 Voting in Oklahoma's 2026 midterms? Here's what ID you need to bring
 Josh Kelly, The Oklahoman 2026년 10월 28일 수 오후 12:58 UTC 0 The gubernatorial race between frontrunners Cyndi Munson and Mike Mazzei could signal two things to the nation regarding one of the nation's most Trump-loyal states: a commitment to President Donald Trump or a flip of a Republican stronghold state.
 Eyes are on the governor race, but several other state and federal offices are up for election. 
 Early voting locations open Wednesday, Oct. 28, giving voters a chance to cast their ballots ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3. But before Oklahomans can cast their ballots, each voter must provide the proper identification.
 Here's what you need to know to vote in Oklahoma's midterm election this year.
 What do I need to vote in election?
 All voters must provide proof of identity to vote in Oklahoma. Identity can be proven in three different ways, according to the Oklahoma State Election Board:
 Photo identification . This needs to be a document issued by the United States government (REAL ID), the State of Oklahoma (State ID) or a federally recognized tribal government. It must have the voter's name, a photo and must not have expired before Nov. 3.
 County Election Board Voter Identification Card . The County Election Board sends a free voter identification card by mail after each voter has registered to vote which can be used.
 Affidavit with provisional ballot . Provisional ballots can be used if a voter does not wish or is unable to show proof of identity. Check with the local Election Board.
 What's on my ballot?
 Each voter's ballot will contain the local races they're eligible to vote on.
 Advertisement
 Use the  OK Voter Portal  to view your sample ballot.
 Early voting in Oklahoma
 In-person absentee voting, also known as early voting, begins Wednesday, Oct. 28 , for the Nov. 3 runoff election.
 Early voting locations will be open on these dates and times to allow extra time for voters to cast their ballots:
 Wednesday, Oct. 28: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
 Thursday, Oct. 29: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
 Friday, Oct. 30: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
 Saturday, Oct. 31: 8 a.m. to 2 p.m.
 During the General Election, Oklahoma County voters can cast their vote early at one of three locations, including:
 Mac Center - 2733 Marilyn Williams Dr. in Edmond
 Oklahoma County Election Board - 4201 N Lincoln Blvd in Oklahoma City
 The Rock Church - 6801 S Anderson Rd in Oklahoma City
 A list of early voting locations around the state, as well as sample ballots or voter registration information, is available at the State Election Board  website , http://hosting.okelections.gov/earlyvote.html .
